headline: Growth hits multi-year high as profitability scales
summary_short: Revenue rose 20% y/y to $1,407M in Q1 FY2026 — Twilio's highest growth rate in over three years — as Dollar-Based Net Expansion hit 114% and GAAP operating income more than quadrupled y/y to $108M.
summary_long: Revenue grew 20% y/y to $1,407M, driven by higher usage from existing customers (DBNE 114%), $70.9M from new accounts, and $46.1M of pass-through A2P fees. Cost of revenue rose 22% on higher network provider costs, but gross profit still grew 18%. Opex rose just 3% against 20% revenue growth, driving GAAP operating income up more than fourfold y/y to $108M and net income to $90M ($0.57 diluted EPS) from $20M. Twilio repurchased $253.4M of stock, with $892.0M still authorized. Free cash flow fell to $132M (9% margin) from $178M (15%), mainly on a $141.0M bonus-program payout in March 2026. Twilio initiated Q2 2026 guidance ($1.420-$1.430B revenue) and raised FY2026 revenue-growth guidance to 14%-15% from 11.5%-12.5%.

drivers.explanation: CEO Khozema Shipchandler called Q1 "a milestone quarter" with the highest revenue and gross-profit growth rates in over three years, attributing it to a multi-year push on innovation velocity, go-to-market efficiency, and financial rigor.

Growth was primarily attributable to increased usage by existing customers (DBNE of 114%), $70.9M from new customer accounts, and $46.1M in incremental A2P messaging fees newly introduced by major U.S. carriers.

Cost of revenue rose 22% (mainly $118.1M higher network service provider costs, net of hedging, including the $46.1M A2P pass-through), slightly outpacing revenue growth in percentage terms but still lifting gross profit dollars 18%.
Total operating expenses rose only 3% (R&D +3%, S&M roughly flat, G&A +11%) against 20% revenue growth, driving the sharp operating-margin expansion.

Net income growth tracks the operating-income gain; other (expenses) income swung to a $5.4M expense from $3.5M income, mainly a $7.8M increase in equity-method investment losses, but pretax income growth still outpaced it.
EPS growth combines the net-income increase with a lower weighted diluted share count (158M vs 162M a year ago), reflecting the ongoing buyback program.
This shard-sourced figure tracks the same revenue and cost drivers as GAAP operating income above; it is a third-party derivation, not the company's own non-GAAP operating-income figure.

The y/y decline was driven by a $149.3M decrease in accounts payable and other current liabilities, primarily from paying $141.0M under the 2025 companywide bonus program in March 2026, which outweighed the higher net income.
Cash fell q/q mainly on $253.4M of share repurchases and the $141.0M bonus payout, partly offset by $153.2M of operating cash flow; not fully itemized by the release beyond these two flows.

Not directly explained in the release; the q/q decline likely reflects treasury-stock reductions from the $253.4M of share repurchases, partly offset by $90.1M of net income and stock-based compensation.
Diluted share count fell y/y (158M vs 162M) as the ongoing $2.0B share repurchase program outpaced new share issuance from equity-plan settlements.
